subject: [PATCH v2] memcg: Don't call schedule_work when no spinning is allowed

reviews.author: David Stevens
reviews.summary: Reviewer David Stevens noted that the patch's fix for RT kernels is incorrect because it will execute as part of css_free_rwork_fn() which is not under cgroup_mutex, and suggested using IRQ_WORK_INIT_HARD instead of init_irq_work() in mem_cgroup_alloc()
reviews.raw_body:
This executes as part of css_free_rwork_fn(), so it isn't under cgroup_mutex.

-David

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the use of synchronize_rcu() in css_free_rwork_fn is something to avoid, but not a blocker for this patch; added an Acked-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
Oh yes, css_free_rwork_fn does not take cgroup_mutex. Though synchronize_rcu()
is still something to avoid but not a blocker.

Acked-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>

2026-09-04.patch_summary: This patch modifies the memcg (memory cgroup) code to prevent it from calling schedule_work when spinning is not allowed, which can cause a deadlock on RT kernels by putting the RCU grace period in an inconsistent state while holding the cgroup_mutex. The fix involves replacing init_irq_work() with IRQ_WORK_INIT_HARD to ensure that high-priority work is properly initialized and scheduled.
